Scene checklists and triage order are learned in context with the crash narrative and need no separate practice mode.

sections.heading: C — Emergencies and collisions
sections.markdown:
## C — Emergencies and collisions

FACT_ID: sec10-F01 | anchor: A41
Build the habit of signaling each direction change, even on empty roads, since a hidden traveler may need your warning. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0041]
FACT_ID: sec10-F02 | anchor: A41
Start the signal at least three seconds before moving, yet hold it until past any streets or driveways short of your turn, like a driveway just past a crossing. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0041]
FACT_ID: sec10-F03 | anchor: A41
When a car is about to enter between you and your turn, signal only after passing it, or it may pull into your path. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0041]
FACT_ID: sec10-F04 | anchor: A41
After finishing a turn or lane change, check the signal is off, since gentle turns may not cancel it and a stray blink invites wrong guesses. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0041]
FACT_ID: sec10-F05 | anchor: A41
Slow as early as safe, and where a stop will surprise followers, tap the brake pedal three or four times: exits without lanes, parking or turning ahead of a crossing, expected turns, or hidden road hazards. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0041]
FACT_ID: sec10-F06 | anchor: A41
When trouble strikes, pull clear of traffic if possible, switch flashers on, alert authorities, and if stuck on the road, halt where sight lines are long, never just past a hill or curve. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0041]
FACT_ID: sec10-F07 | anchor: A41
Set flares behind a stalled car so lanes can shift; without flares, wave traffic by from a safe shoulder with a white cloth, raise the hood or tie cloth to the antenna, mirror or handle, and never stand or change tires in a lane. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0041]
FACT_ID: sec10-F08 | anchor: A41
With dead brakes, pump the pedal hard, then ease the parking brake on slowly without locking the rear wheels, releasing at any skid, and if still rolling, drop gears and coast to a safe off-road stop, never driving on. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0041]
FACT_ID: sec10-F09 | anchor: A41
On a sudden flat, grip the wheel tight, hold straight, lift off the gas, brake lightly, and roll to a safe shoulder instead of halting in the road. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0041]
FACT_ID: sec10-F10 | anchor: A42
If the engine quits moving, keep a firm grip though steering turns heavy, steer off the road, and press the brake pedal very hard to stop. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0042]
FACT_ID: sec10-F11 | anchor: A42
When headlights die, slow gently, leave the road fast, flick the switch a few tries, then run flashers, signals or fog lamps, and do not keep driving. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0042]
FACT_ID: sec10-F12 | anchor: A42
If the motor races on its own, eyes forward, shift quickly to neutral, pull off when clear, and kill the engine. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0042]
FACT_ID: sec10-F13 | anchor: A42
Never twist the ignition to lock while rolling, or the wheel freezes and control is gone. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0042]
FACT_ID: sec10-F14 | anchor: A42
A crash can almost always be dodged or softened, with three answers to pick from: stop, turn, or speed up. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0042]
FACT_ID: sec10-F15 | anchor: A42
With antilock brakes, push the pedal down as hard as you can and hold through any pushback, since easing off kills the system. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0042]
FACT_ID: sec10-F16 | anchor: A42
Without antilock brakes, brake hard short of locking, and at the first skid, lift fast, then press again, repeating until halted. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0042]
FACT_ID: sec10-F17 | anchor: A42
A car usually turns sooner than it stops, so grip with both hands, aim where you want to go, hold control after the swerve to dodge a second crash, and with antilock brakes you may brake and turn together. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0042]
FACT_ID: sec10-F18 | anchor: A42
Without antilock brakes, brake first, release, then turn, loading the front tires for a tighter arc without locking them or cutting so sharp the car plows ahead; leaving the road beats meeting another car head-on. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0042]
FACT_ID: sec10-F19 | anchor: A42
Sometimes the escape is forward gas, when a side or rear strike looms and open road waits ahead; ease off once past the danger. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0042]
FACT_ID: sec10-F20 | anchor: A42
Skids strike when tires outrun their grip, on wet or icy roads or simply too fast for the bend, and a sliding car answers no command, so prevention wins. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0042]
FACT_ID: sec10-F21 | anchor: A42
In a skid, stay off the brake until speed bleeds down, steer toward your target, unwind the wheel as the car straightens to block a swing the other way, and keep correcting left and right until it tracks true. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0042]
FACT_ID: sec10-F22 | anchor: A43
Pass others’ crashes by unless you are part of them or no help has come, and never detour to stare, since rubberneckers choke the path of police, fire, ambulance and tow crews. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0043]
FACT_ID: sec10-F23 | anchor: A43
Join a crash and you must halt, hunt down a parked car’s owner, call police for any injury or death, and know that slipping away before officers finish is a crime. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0043]
FACT_ID: sec10-F24 | anchor: A43
Belts come first against crash injury, lap plus shoulder every seat, and a stocked kit of flares, first aid and basic tools rides along for the aftermath. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0043]
FACT_ID: sec10-F25 | anchor: A43
Braced for a rear strike, pin yourself to the seatback, rest your head on the restraint, and stand on the brakes so the shove cannot launch you onward. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0043]
FACT_ID: sec10-F26 | anchor: A43
A side slam flings you toward the blow, where front airbags give no aid, so belts must hold you at the wheel while you steer or brake against the next impact. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0043]
FACT_ID: sec10-F27 | anchor: A43
Meeting a frontal crash, twist for a glancing blow over a square hit, ride out the airbag’s burst and fall, and let the belts pin you for a possible second strike. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0043]
FACT_ID: sec10-F28 | anchor: A43
At the scene, park at its edge and clear of lanes, kill every wreck’s ignition, smoke nothing near spilled fuel, shun fallen wires, and flare the road so traffic skirts the wreckage. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0043]
FACT_ID: sec10-F29 | anchor: A43
For the hurt, summon police and medics, naming any fire, move nobody unless flames or traffic threaten, aid the silent ones first checking breath then blood, press wounds hard with hand or cloth, give no drink even water, and wrap the shocked in coats against the chill. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0043]
FACT_ID: sec10-F30 | anchor: A43
Trade names, addresses, license numbers, plate, make, model, year and insurance details with all drivers and witnesses, log the damage, answer officers fully, pin a dated note with your contact on an unfound parked car, and always file with police when hurt, killed or property breaks. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0043]
